utterances.text: Witness, did Mr. Kojic achieve later on a position in the government of the SAO Eastern Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He became the Defence Minister of that region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did a meeting take place in mid-July 1991 attended by a former policeman from Vukovar, and if so, what -- how did this meeting come about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: I'm sorry but I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did a meeting take place in mid-July attended by the former policeman of Vukovar with Mr. Hadzic, and can you tell us why you met?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes, it did. Not one former policeman but all the former policemen - that's why I didn't understand your question - and Mr. Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Can you explain what happened at this meeting? Why was it conducted in the first place, and what was said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: At the meeting, what was supposed to have happened was to elect the secretary of internal affairs or, rather, the secretariat for internal affairs, for the interior, for the Vukovar municipality, people who had been in exile or, rather, in Borovo Selo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean a police -- a police force was to be established, a police force in Borovo Selo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes. That's precisely what it meant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was it supposed to be a civilian police with the usual civilian tasks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes, a civilian police with civilian tasks. That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that an initiative by the policemen who attended the meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: No. First of all, I think that this initiative came from the people, and this reached Mr. Goran Hadzic. And also I think that it was dictated from Serbia as well that this should be done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why do you think that? Did you have -- did you hear anything to that effect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: I think that because it was precisely in talking to Kojic, and Mr. Ante before that, that the time had come for this to be done, because in Borovo Selo, some strange things were happening at that time. The people had been armed to a considerable degree, and the people quite Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. simply wanted to have peace reign as much as possible, and they wanted to have a regular police force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, this Ante, this person Ante, did you find out his correct name, his full name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes, I did, later on. His name was Radovan Kostic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he an official of the Serbian DB?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, we need to go into private session because I would like to address point 11 in the summary.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time when the civil police was established in July 1991, was there already another sort of police operating in Borovo Selo and, if so, what kind of people were they and who commanded them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes. There was the so-called village police, men who were simply not capable of doing their job. And personally, I believe that they were under the TO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was their commander and why do you believe they were under the TO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: The commander was Soskocanin himself. And after his death -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. after his death, they acted on their own, more or less. There was no one else there except the TO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have -- did they also have their equipment and weapons from the MUP Serbia? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does "No" mean? You don't know that or they didn't have their weapons from the MUP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: They didn't have them. They had weapons that was coming illegally across the Danube.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean they came as you described it before, how they came over the river and were then -- through the Sarac person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The civilian police that was established, did they have problems with this so-called -- with this other police which was under the TO? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes indeed. We had a lot of problems, serious problems. Those men felt that that was their village, they were the most important there, and we were simply outsiders, regardless of the fact that people from the police had been elected from their own village, that had been selected from the villagers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The civilian police, was it stationed in the TO headquarters or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: No. The civilian police had its own separate premises that were given to them by the TO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the civilian police cooperate with the TO, and, if so, were there any problems?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes, they did cooperate. They had to cooperate. And in those days, there weren't any problems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the civilian police cooperate with the JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: No. With the JNA it did not cooperate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would now like to turn to you -- to the attack on Dalj in August 1991. When did the attack on Dalj occur? Do you know the date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes, I do. On the 1st of August, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like now to go into private session on paragraph 17 of the proofing summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And I think we can stay in open session for a while and as long as the witness does not refer to the meeting that he just described before the break.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, during your talks with me and investigators in preparation of your testimony, did you make annotations onto a map of the region that is concerned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can the witness please be given the Exhibit 326, tab 15.C13. Is this the map that you discussed and on which you made these annotations in different colours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we have it on the ELMO, and I would like you to explain a few things. Before the attack on Dalj, were the Serb-controlled areas like it is here, in -- shown in brown, in this light brown? Is that what you indicated are the Serb-controlled areas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please point out Borovo Selo on the ELMO with the pointer. On the ELMO, please, not on the screen. Would you please point out Borovo Selo.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these pink-coloured zones, were these villages that were controlled by Croats?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please point out Dalj.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. And you have here indicated in green a line around that whole territory between more or less Osijek and Vukovar, including Vukovar, actually. Is that the territory that was talked about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you have also indicated here a blue line. When was -- what does that mean, the blue line? Can you explain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: The blue line was the area that was not under control, and the green was later on, when all of that was established. This is what should have been linked up. These places needed to be linked up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. So just to clarify, the -- when you look at the map on the legend, it says there for green, "Hadzic's plan," and blue it says, "End result." And I would like to know from you when was this entire territory that you have encircled in blue, when was it under the control of the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Around mid-October or the end of October.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When it comes to dates, how -- how well do you remember dates? Can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Not very well at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which town was attacked first within this territory, within this encircled territory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: It would be better to say "village."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Which village was attacked first?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: The village of Dalj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you have indicated here with red -- red arrows movements, and the first red arrow you have put between Borovo Selo and Dalj, and you have also marked here the word "TO." Can you explain how the attack on Dalj was actually conducted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Units of the TO set off from Borovo Selo towards Dalj. They were formed into three groups. The first group, which used military vehicles and entered Dalj, attacked the police station. The second group attacked members of the ZNG and the guards in the area of the water supply system, and a third group that accompanied them and that did not take part in the fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did the attack start, and was it in any way provoked by actions of the Croats in Dalj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: The attack started in the morning, on the 1st of August, around 4.00 a.m. And there were no provocations on the part of Croatian members of either the army or the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have also indicated on the map an arrow, a red arrow, and you have written there "JNA." It's in the right-hand corner. Can you explain how the JNA got involved in the attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes. Members of the JNA were in that area that I have indicated, and this was the bridge between Erdut in Bogojevo. And after the attack, after the first shots were fired, those units joined in. A part of them came to Dalj directly and joined in the fighting, providing assistance to the TO members, and a second group went in the direction of Erdut and Carvak -- Palmas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you indicate Erdut and Palmas on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Aljmas. Erdut, Aljmas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean Erdut was attacked on that same day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The JNA, did they come from -- it looks here -- did they come from Serbia? Did they get involved coming over the bridge from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes, because there's no other road except across that bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did the attack last?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: A few hours, as far as I can remember. By noon, everything was over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the population of Dalj and Erdut and the region, what did happen in relation to the population?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Could you please clarify? Which population do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean the Croatian population.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: The Croatian population was leaving their homes in Dalj and Erdut, in the Dalj mountain, and was fleeing in the direction of Aljmas. In those days, Croatia had already organised, that is, the Croatian army and the police. They came along the Drava River in boats, and all these people were transported to Osijek along the Drava River Valley -- river, sorry. Drava River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This region was under Croatian control?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Up until the 1st of August, until 4.00 a.m., Dalj, Erdut, the Dalj mountain, Aljmas were under Croatian control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But I was asking about where the population fled to on the 1st of August. Did they flee to Croat-held territory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were Croats also driven out forcefully on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did that, and in which way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: The TO members, with the full support of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did they do? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Would you repeat that, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did they do? You said that the people were driven out forcefully by the TO in full support of the JNA. In which way was that achieved?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: When the police station was attacked in Dalj, there were many casualties, many casualties on the Croatian side. There was a lot of shooting, and people realised what was happening and started to flee. And as -- when the JNA crossed the bridge, some of them went in the direction of Erdut. Let me just point out that everyone was armed in those days, both Serbs and Croats. The Croats put up resistance in Erdut, as much as they could, which wasn't of such great significance for the JNA, because they entered the area in armoured vehicles so that they didn't have much choice but to flee in the direction of Aljmas and to go along the Drava River to Osijek as best they could.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have indicated quite a few Croat settlements here in that encircled territory. When the operations in the regions were terminated, were all these settlements gone? Were all the Croats gone from this region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes. They left. From most of these villages, yes, they left, with the exception of the Dalj mountain, Corkovac, where the villages were mostly inhabited by ethnic Hungarians. As they didn't want to, at least, most of them didn't wish to take weapons either from the Serbs or the Croats, they felt that they did no wrong and that they could stay in their homes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the attacks, the subsequent attacks, on the region, can you say in which direction and in which order was the whole -- the whole region taken? Where did the forces move?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: I can. On that day, the JNA and the TO stopped at the border between Sarvas and Bijelo Brdo. And during the two or two and a half months that we are referring to, these lines moved forward until they reached the end of this green or, rather, blue line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was it always done in a similar fashion, that is, TO attacking first and then the JNA moving in, or how was that done in the other places? Was it similar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: As for the other places, I really can't say. I don't know much about that, because I was there in the area for some time. But more or less while I was there up until October, the line went this way, in this direction.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. I would like to turn briefly again to that meeting that we had discussed and, therefore, would like to ask for private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While the secretariat functioned in Dalj, did the supplies continue to come from the MUP Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Milan Martic visit Dalj in August 1991? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes, I do know something about that. I personally greeted him and talked to him because I knew him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did he meet in Dalj? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: He had a meeting with Hadzic and, I think, all the members -- rather, not members but all the commanders of the Territorial Defence were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were not present? You did not take part in the meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: I did take part.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I think we need to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, was there a prison facility in Borovo Selo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that there was a prison in Borovo Selo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was it established and how long did it exist?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: When it was established, I don't know, but I assume sometime in May 1991. And it continued to exist after I left the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did you leave the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: I left at the end of October.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who ran it? Who ran that prison facility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: The TO ran it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you say anything about the size and capacity and how many people were detained there in the months from August to October?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: This was a cinema hall which was equipped for that purpose, and as the Croatian villages were taken control of one by one, so Croats were brought to that prison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Civilians or soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Not soldiers, no. Civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they mistreated, to your knowledge? Were they mistreated during their detention there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: I can't say that. I never went to the prison. I had no right to. But only on a couple of occasions I passed by when those people were working outside. They were carrying wheat and maize. They were working. They had guards, TO guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you. We wouldn't need these details. So you don't know about mistreatment. That was my question. Was there a prison in --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a prison in Dalj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was it situated and who ran it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Again, it was run by the TO, and it was situated -- I could point out the place to you, but I can't tell you exactly. Anyway, close to the Orthodox church in Dalj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what kind of a place was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: What place?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. What kind of a building was it; a normal house or a police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Next to that building was a police station, was the police station. Maybe the distance between them was 20 or 30 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in which time did it operate? Do you know that? Was that the same period, August until you left at least?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes. The prison was set up on the same day as the police station, which means after the 1st of August.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were Croats detained there; in particular, civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you know how many were detained there in Dalj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: I really don't know. I have to say again that I was never in that prison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether detainees were mistreated there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes, I do know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Were they -- in which way were they mistreated, and how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: I know because the commander would submit reports to me as to what was happening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: What happened was that Arkan would come to the prison and take people away wherever he wanted to.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, we come to this, because we have two documents to this effect, we come to this a little bit later. This Arkan section follows.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, just one question in private session in relation to the prisons.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I would like to now go to paragraph 34.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Arkan arrive in the region about the same time as Zavisic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he come with a group of men? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes, he did, in several vans with markings of Arkan's Tigers. And this is my information. I think there weren't more than 50 or 60 members with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did they put up their headquarters in Erdut, in the winery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Arkan's men in Dalj and recognise them due to their special uniforms and their vehicles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes, I saw his men many times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were their uniforms like? What is special that you can recognise them immediately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Those were black uniforms, completely black, uniforms that were well-supplied with headphones, radio transmitters, first-class weaponry, and all the equipment that befits an elite or special policeman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of weapons did they have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: They mostly had Hecklers, and it is known that this is a very fast-operating weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, were there roadblocks and checkpoints in the region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes. From the first day there were barricades between the villages which were not removed even later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could Arkan and his men, could they move throughout these checkpoints without any problems?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Those checkpoints did not exist as far as Arkan was concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who actually manned those checkpoints; police, TO, JNA, or all three?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: At first the TO. Later, when the villages had been linked together, it was taken over by the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While Arkan was in the region, did he recruit men into his special Tiger group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, quite a number of men, in fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How strong did the force around Arkan grow while you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but since they were to be seen everywhere in the area, I can freely say that at least 300 or 400.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they local people or did they come from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: No, they were not local people. Those people came from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Arkan at that time from public sources, and did he have a reputation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes. I knew Arkan from before. Not personally, but I knew him from police documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a criminal? Did he have a criminal reputation and police records?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes. We can quite freely say that he was not only -- that he not only had a police record in Yugoslavia but also in Interpol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he arrived in the region with his men, did his men commit any crimes such as looting? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: We had many reported thefts on the part of Arkan and his men. Those lootings occurred mostly in the area of Erdut, the Dalj mountain, Aljmas, which means in the places that I mentioned before and in which I said earlier on that people remained who had not wanted to take up weapons either from the Serbs or the Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean the victims of these activities were mostly Hungarians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes. That is precisely what that means.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this group around Arkan, did they have a special pattern in which they conducted such lootings? And in this regard, I would like to refer to the villages Laslovo and Korodj.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Korodj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand the question, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When Arkan's men looted, did they have a special way how they did it? Did they have a special pattern of conduct? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes. The method was that they would enter at night into a house and carry out valuables, demanding money. Many of those people would come to report this secretly so that nobody knew about it. However, the police at the time was simply powerless to do anything because Mr. Zavisic had determined that in -- that the regular police could not be dispatched to those areas, so that they simply could not protect those people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Arkan and -- you mentioned already that Arkan and Zavisic actually shared a headquarters or the same premises. Did they cooperate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes. I saw them together on many an occasion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the civilian police get involved, participate in combat activities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: No. No. They really never did participate in combat activities. But I have to add by members of the police -- among the police members, there were some who simply neglected their role as policemen. They found it boring. And people like that left the police and joined the TO headquarters or some other formations, and then they continued their activities there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the civilian police called upon by the TO to participate in an attack on Borovo Naselje in September 1991, and what did the police do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-013
utterances.text: Yes, that is true. The police did not take part. It was rejected.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would now go into -- I would have to go to private session because we come now to several meetings with Arkan, Stanisic, and those kind of people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that's a convenient moment. We will adjourn now.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: My assumption is that I will need another approximately half an hour. It may be a little bit more because it's going a little bit slow, but I can't do anything about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We'll sit again at 9.00 tomorrow morning. We will adjourn until then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
